summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — FME.DE +2%, ULVR.L +2%, CCEP.L +2%, UNA.AS +2%, HNR1.DE +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (STMPA.PA -11%, ASML.AS -9%, PCT.L -8%, G24.DE -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: STMPA.PA (-10.81%) — No company-specific news found; reports point to a broad tech/semiconductor selloff, with STMicro the CAC 40's worst performer (down ~6.5% at midday, closed -10.8%). Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: STMPA.PA is a Euronext Paris large-cap semiconductor name that no strategy includes. A sector-wide drift with no earnings or news trigger also gives a news-reactive bot nothing to act on.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news. Likely a rebound after the Nov 12 Fresenius SE placement at €39 (stake cut to ~20%) and ongoing FME buyback support. Cause is unverified.

top_movers.suggestion: No strong change warranted. If a German healthcare name should be eligible, add a Xetra mid-cap healthcare tier to the mean-reversion universe, gated on ADV and a ≥2% move with a volume-ratio check.

top_movers.suggestion: No change to the trust itself. Instead, add a tech-sector drawdown signal (e.g. a Nasdaq-100 -2% day flag) that tightens momentum entries on US tech names, since PCT's move is derivative of its holdings.
